description: SQL-DEMAND, missing variant: which population boundary ADO's recordset events expose for each query shape. For a plain scan, ORDER BY, GROUP BY, DISTINCT, TOP 10 with ORDER BY and a crosstab over Nm (256 rows), each on its own ADODB.Recordset with the recording sink connected to RecordsetEvents before Open (static cursor, read-only), then RecordCount, MoveLast, MoveFirst, MoveNext twice and Close; and the plain scan and the sort once more with a forward-only cursor, read by MoveNext three times. Asks which events (WillMove, MoveComplete, FetchProgress, FetchComplete, EndOfRecordset, WillChangeRecordset, RecordsetChangeComplete) arrive, with which arguments, in which order relative to each call and on which thread. Follow-up probe (round 2) for SQL-DEMAND; works on a fresh writable copy of fixture r-q2-expr-sql-main. Each DAO statement is preceded by a marker (a DROP TABLE of a table that does not exist, which always fails), so DBEngine.Errors read after the statement shows that statement's own failure or the marker's, never an older one.
retentionNote: Designed r-q2-expr-sql probe (A-02); complete capture of the ACE answer.
